messages:

Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@acmetech.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: view-only access for penetration test deliverables / redaction scope

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this — Acme Tech is preparing for our SOC 2 Type II audit and the auditor team has requested access to the full penetration test deliverables (findings, evidence snippets, and remediation validation). We understand Redwood redacts sensitive infra details for customer safety; the auditors need to validate remediation and the timelines.

Could you confirm whether Redwood can provide:
- A signed NDA (legal approved) ahead of sharing;
- A view-only, time-bound viewer for the full report + evidence (watermarked, no download); and
- A short redaction sniplist so our auditors know what was removed versus what remains.

If possible, please send a proposed redaction sniplist and the NDA — auditors are scheduled to start the week of 11/22.

Appreciate the help — happy to sync by call if that helps.

Thanks,
Derek
Derek Hall
Security Assurance Manager, Acme Tech

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@acmetech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: view-only access for penetration test deliverables / redaction scope

Hi Derek —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can support auditor validation while protecting sensitive operational details. Proposed approach:

1) Exec summary (PDF) — redacted for infra-specific identifiers but preserves vulnerability IDs, risk level, and remediation status.
2) Time-bound secure viewer — hosted link, watermark by viewer session, no download/print, session logs exported for audit evidence.
3) Redaction sniplist (draft attached) — shows categories we will strip (internal hostnames, cloud account IDs, exact ephemeral tokens) and what we leave (vuln ID, CVSS, evidence excerpt with context, remediation ticket ref).
4) DocuSign NDA — we have a standard "restricted disclosure" addendum for pen test materials; Marissa (legal) is on-copy to finalize.

Attached: redaction_sniplist_draft.xlsx (this is a living doc — please flag any items you consider blockers for your auditors).

If auditors need raw packet captures or PII that we redacted, we can consider a controlled escrow process; would need a security technical point of contact and explicit sampling criteria.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Marissa will send NDA redline;
- Karthik will provide a remediation tracker with closure dates;
- We will queue the viewer environment and send access once the NDA is executed.

Would you prefer Redline NDA via DocuSign or we share a downloadable Word for your legal to redline and return?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Trust & Security — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: view-only access for penetration test deliverables / redaction scope

Hi Derek,

I've attached a redline of our standard Viewer NDA (NDA_Redline_v2.docx). Key calls in the redline:
- We allow auditor access under an executed NDA with a narrowing clause: access only for named auditor entities and only for the SOC2 engagement window.
- We maintain carveouts for high-sensitivity artifacts (full stack traces with internal hostnames, private keys, internal IAM identifiers).
- We propose a watermarking + session logging requirement and a 90-day post-access embargo for redistribution.
- For escrowed evidence (if required): evidence will be provided to the named auditor under strict chain-of-custody and ephemeral credentials; Redwood will require an auditor attestation form confirming evidence handling.

Please review the redline and let me know if your legal team has specific clauses to propose. If you prefer, we can route this for DocuSign execution; I've prefilled the auditor-named-party slots as placeholders.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

If Acme needs escrowed raw artifacts we will need to coordinate SOW for secure transfer and an on-call engineer for evidence handover — I can be that point.
